business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stevedoring and Loading/Unloading of Bulk Cargo at Marine Docks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, signed 30 May 1985
Convention between France and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital, signed 31 August 1994, as amended by the 2006 Protocol

Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49 to 55, concerning the freedom of establishment and cross-border corporate structuring
Convention between France and Hong Kong for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Income and Capital Gains, signed 22 April 2010
EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement, in force 14 February 2021, as applicable to French-Singapore investment relations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Governing instruments: (1) Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Book V, Title VI, Articles L561-1 to L561-57 and R561-1 to R561-24, governing AML/CFT obligations, beneficial owner declarations and TRACFIN reporting; (2) Law No. 2016-731 of 3 June 2016 (Sapin II); (3) Décret No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 establishing the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) maintained within the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS/INPI); (4) Ordonnance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); (5) Directive (EU) 2024/1640 (6AMLD) with phased implementation obligations applicable by 2027; (6) Port-specific operating licence requirements under Code des transports, Articles L5351-7 and R5351-11 (licence de manutention portuaire).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each individual shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or accredited notary of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or equivalent company extract (Kbis-equivalent) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certificate of corporate existence for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate affairs registrar or equivalent supervisory authority of the origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (pouvoir) appointing the local incorporator and domiciliary agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identification document of each proposed director of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identification authority of the director's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of lawful origin of funds for each contributing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed banking institution holding the contributor's account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French documents by a court-appointed sworn translator (traducteur assermenté)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court of Appeal recognized translator registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation accompanied by source-document Hague Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors and ultimate beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, French national asset-freezing list, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction bulletins. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are defined under CMF Article L561-10(1) and FATF Recommendations 12 and 22, covering present and former senior political office-holders, including domestic and foreign PEPs, with a 12-month cooling-off period for foreign PEPs and enhanced due diligence for domestic PEPs where a higher risk profile is identified. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, high-risk third countries, and complex or unusual transaction structures; continuous transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting to TRACFIN apply under CMF Articles L561-15 and L561-25.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, underpinned by the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) database at data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may employ any language expressed in Latin script, but the articles of association (statuts) must be drafted in French pursuant to Article 1834 of the Code civil. Foreign-language names must be transliterated into Latin characters, must not contravene French public order (ordre public) or good morals, and must be distinguishable from pre-existing RNCS entries, prior INPI trademark registrations, and protected geographical indications.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must first obtain the written grounds of refusal from the INPI/registrar. The applicant may (i) refile an amended name application through the Guichet unique within 15 days of rejection; (ii) submit a formal administrative appeal to the INPI in accordance with the Code des relations entre le public et l'administration (CRPA) within 30 days of the refusal; and (iii) if administrative remedies fail, institute summary proceedings (référé) before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce based on the intended registered office within 15 days of the second refusal. Each appeal step is subject to filing fees ranging from EUR 25 to EUR 75.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual or domiciled offices are permissible solely for administrative seat purposes: the SAS may be domiciled with a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) for a maximum period of five years under Article L123-11-2 of the Code de commerce. However, the stevedoring operating licence (licence de manutention portuaire) under Articles L5351-7 and R5351-11 of the Code des transports requires an operational base, working equipment, and a genuine and permanent local establishment inside or immediately adjacent to the port perimeter; a virtual office alone does not satisfy the port authority's commercial substance and safety requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High quantified risk, estimated at 70% to 80% within the first 18 months of operation, due to unannounced on-site inspections by the Grand Port Maritime, port safety commission, French customs, labour inspectorate (inspection du travail), and DGITM maritime safety services for bulk stevedoring terminal operations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance and RNCS availability search (INPI / Guichet unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff, fixed fee of EUR 38.81 equivalent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS articles of association (statuts) and corporate counsel review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 2,000 to EUR 3,000 fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of the UBO and shareholder document bundle (3-5 documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of EUR 80 to EUR 110 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn English-French certified translation of foreign corporate and shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory market benchmark of EUR 60 to EUR 90 per standard page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the legal incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a legal announcements gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) of the relevant jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated tariff of approximately EUR 150 per publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing (formalités de création) through the Guichet unique and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff of approximately EUR 43 to EUR 76, plus registration fees of EUR 50 to EUR 200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (RBE) preparation and filing with the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm, with disbursement to the RCS Greffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 200 fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service under Article L123-11-2 of the Code de commerce (one-year subscription)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 600 to EUR 900 per annum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial AML/CFT compliance program, PEP screening architecture and KYC onboarding setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance counsel or specialized AML service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 4,000 to EUR 5,500 including port authority dossier fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing sociétés par actions simplifiées; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. governing registration; Articles L.561-46 et seq. governing beneficial-owner disclosure; applicable provisions of the Civil Code for contracts, contributions, and registered-office arrangements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE) and the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) maintained by the competent commercial court registry or tribunal des activités économiques registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application for immatriculation of a société par actions simplifiée to the RNE and RCS through the Guichet unique, accompanied by the signed statuts, beneficial-owner declaration, registered-office evidence, and incorporation notices.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to a SAS. The amount is determined by the statuts. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon subscription, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must generally be fully released at incorporation. Cash funds are deposited in a blocked account with a French bank, notary, or authorized deposit institution and released after registration against the Kbis extract. The amount excludes the legal-notice publication fee, beneficial-owner filing fee, professional fees, and any applicable chamber or sector charges.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts and records the subscription by the founding shareholder(s) for the shares specified in the incorporation documents, with cash contributions deposited in accordance with applicable law; RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full address, France], effective upon registration; RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed President for an unlimited term, subject to the statuts, and that [name] is appointed, where applicable, as Directeur Général; RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to complete all filings, publish required notices, open operating bank accounts, and execute documents necessary to commence the Company’s activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate name, activity, registered office, and port location
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; relevant port authority or Grand Port Maritime; competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve or verify the corporate name, identify the precise port terminal and activities, confirm the registered-office right of use, and distinguish the corporate registered office from the operational terminal. Obtain written evidence of domicile, lease, domiciliation agreement, or owner consent. Confirm that the proposed stevedoring activity is compatible with the port concession, terminal agreement, land-use rules, and port regulations.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and trading name
Description of stevedoring, bulk-cargo handling, storage, and ancillary activities
Registered-office lease, domiciliation agreement, or owner consent
Port site identification and preliminary authorization or concession documentation
Identification documents and addresses of shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the activity wording, address evidence, or name issue through the Guichet unique response process. If the registry rejects the filing, submit the requested evidence within the stated deadline and, where necessary, seek clarification from the registry or challenge the decision under applicable commercial-court procedural rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SAS articles and shareholder instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders, French counsel or notary where required, and the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, specifying the name, form, purpose, registered office, share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance powers, President, financial year, and dissolution rules. Execute the statuts electronically or by wet signature. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary SAS incorporation; use a notarial deed where real-estate contributions or another legally notarial transaction is involved. Foreign signatories should provide legalized or apostilled powers of attorney and certified French translations where required.
required_dossiers: Signed SAS statuts
Share subscription and contribution schedule
Shareholder identification and corporate authority documents
Foreign corporate certificates of incorporation and incumbency, if applicable
Apostilled or legalized powers of attorney, if applicable
French translations by an appropriately qualified translator, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify execution defects, incomplete signatures, missing powers, or translation deficiencies and circulate an amended or restated set of statuts. Re-execute the documents before resubmission if the registry identifies an authority or signature defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscribe capital and obtain the deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, authorized deposit institution, or French notary; Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, submit the executed statuts and subscriber information, transfer the cash subscription, and obtain the certificat du dépositaire des fonds. Record any balance payable after incorporation. For contributions in kind, obtain a commissaire aux apports report unless a statutory exemption is validly elected and documented. Do not treat operational working capital as paid-up capital unless legally subscribed and deposited as share capital.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts and subscription schedule
Subscriber identity and beneficial-owner information
Bank compliance and source-of-funds documents
Capital deposit instruction and transfer evidence
Certificat du dépositaire des fonds
Commissaire aux apports report or documented exemption, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC or source-of-funds queries, correct subscriber information, and obtain a replacement deposit certificate if the filing data changes. If incorporation fails, request return of funds under the depositary’s procedures and correct the corporate package before a new deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-announcement publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish an avis de constitution in an authorized journal of legal announcements or an authorized online legal-announcement service. Ensure that the notice states the legal form, name, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President, and relevant transfer or admission provisions required for the SAS. Obtain the attestation de parution and preserve the final published text.
required_dossiers: Final signed statuts
Required incorporation notice text
President and officer appointment details
Attestation de parution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice where mandatory information is omitted or inaccurate, and upload the corrected attestation with an explanatory note if the registry has already queried the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the electronic incorporation and beneficial-owner filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select SAS incorporation, enter the principal activity and establishment data, upload the statuts, registered-office evidence, deposit certificate, publication attestation, officer declarations, and beneficial-owner declaration, then pay the displayed charges and retain the filing receipt. Declare all direct and indirect natural-person beneficial owners and the ownership or control basis. Ensure that the registered office, principal establishment, NAF activity, capital, officers, and shareholder data are consistent across all documents.
required_dossiers: Electronic immatriculation application
Signed statuts
Certificat du dépositaire des fonds
Attestation de parution
Registered-office evidence
President and officer declarations of non-conviction and parentage
Identity documents for officers and beneficial owners
Beneficial-owner declaration
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Foreign entity documents and French translations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the Guichet unique or registry query within the prescribed period, upload corrected documents, and keep the filing reference. If the application is rejected, correct the identified defects and resubmit; an appeal or procedural challenge may be made to the competent registry or court where legally available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent RCS registry, INSEE, tax administration, and the company’s bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract, SIREN and SIRET identifiers, and updated RNE information after acceptance. Deliver the Kbis and deposit certificate to the bank to release the capital account and open operating accounts. Confirm tax-account activation, VAT status, payroll registration if employees will be hired, and accounting records. Record the President’s authority limits and establish statutory registers and corporate document controls.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
SIREN, SIRET, and APE/NAF information
RNE registration confirmation
Released-capital bank documents
VAT and tax registration records
Payroll and social-security registration records, if applicable
Corporate registers and accounting opening records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of inaccurate RNE, RCS, INSEE, or tax data through the relevant authority. Escalate unresolved registry discrepancies to the competent registry clerk or court and preserve proof of the original filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete port, industrial, environmental, and operational authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant Grand Port Maritime or port authority; prefecture; DREAL; environmental permitting authority; customs and maritime authorities where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before operations begin, secure the port concession, terminal operating agreement, occupation authorization for the public port domain, and any port police or access approvals. Screen all activities and equipment under the ICPE nomenclature and French Environmental Code. File the applicable declaration, registration, or environmental authorization before construction, storage, handling of regulated substances, emissions, or discharges. Obtain customs, waste, dangerous-goods, maritime-security, and transport approvals where the cargo profile requires them.
required_dossiers: Port concession or terminal operating agreement
Autorisation d'occupation temporaire or equivalent port-domain authorization
Site plan, layout, and equipment schedule
ICPE classification memorandum
Environmental screening and EIA or environmental authorization dossier, if required
Wastewater, stormwater, dust, VOC, and waste-management plans
Dangerous-goods and emergency-response procedures
Customs and maritime-security documentation, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to prefectural, DREAL, port-authority, or environmental queries through the prescribed consultation process. Amend the technical dossier, conduct additional studies, or modify the site design. Use the applicable administrative appeal or litigation route against an adverse authorization decision, while suspending regulated operations until authorization is effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The relevant Grand Port Maritime or local port authority for terminal access, concession, occupation, and operating permissions; the prefecture and Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) for ICPE and environmental regulation; the maritime prefecture for applicable maritime-security and navigation matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Terminal operating agreement or concession and autorisation d'occupation temporaire du domaine public portuaire, supplemented by the applicable port operating authorization and any ICPE declaration, registration, or autorisation environnementale. France does not impose one universal standalone national stevedoring license; the exact authorization package depends on the port, cargo, equipment, storage, and environmental classification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition environmental authorities, including the relevant DREAL and the competent environmental-assessment authority under the French Environmental Code
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening under the Environmental Code. A bulk-cargo terminal may require a full environmental impact assessment and environmental authorization where project size, land works, dredging, storage, emissions, hazardous substances, or ICPE classification meet applicable thresholds. Smaller or lower-risk projects may require prior case-by-case examination, an ICPE declaration or registration, or may be exempt from a full EIA while remaining subject to port, water, waste, and occupational controls.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single universal terminal threshold applies. Wastewater, stormwater, dredging, dust, particulate matter, VOCs, noise, and waste obligations are determined by the applicable ICPE heading, environmental authorization, prefectural order, water-police authorization, port rules, and BAT requirements. Discharges must meet the authorized concentration and load limits and monitoring conditions. Bulk solids require dust suppression and containment controls where required; VOC controls apply to relevant liquid cargoes; hazardous and non-hazardous waste must be segregated, tracked, and transferred to authorized operators, including use of Trackdéchets where legally applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire-safety approval or operational clearance through the competent fire and rescue service (SDIS) and port authority where required; maintain fire-water capacity, emergency access, hazardous-area controls, alarms, extinguishing systems, evacuation plans, and a site emergency plan. Secure building permits and completion or conformity documentation for structures, cranes, silos, conveyors, and storage areas, including structural-load and stability assessments by qualified professionals. Complete workplace risk assessment (document unique), occupational-health arrangements, machinery conformity and periodic inspections, ATEX assessment where explosive atmospheres may arise, lifting-equipment inspections, PPE controls, worker training, and any required consultation or notification to labour authorities and CARSAT.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) for corporate income tax and VAT; customs and export-related matters are administered by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI). Business registration and statutory tax ID procurement are effected through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (entreprendre.service-public.fr) and the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) court greffe.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, the legal representative files the articles of association and constitutive documents via the Guichet Unique with the local RCS court; the Greffe issues the K-bis extract, automatically assigning the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and the definitive French VAT number (FR + INSEE key) after verification by DGFiP. For foreign entities not established in France, a direct VAT registration application is made through the Guichet Unique (or Form 1170 in transitional scenarios); non-EU applicants must appoint an accredited tax representative (représentant fiscal) jointly liable for French VAT. The entity must also obtain an EORI number from DGDDI for customs procedures. The process generally takes between two and six weeks depending on completeness and tax representative accreditation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SAS is a capital company subject to corporate income tax on its worldwide income; permanent establishment exposure is evaluated under French territoriality rules for foreign operations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate US-style check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections relevant to a bulk-port stevedoring SAS include: (i) VAT group election ('assujetti unique') under Article 256 C of the CGI; (ii) French tax consolidation ('intégration fiscale') for groups holding at least 95% of the subsidiary's shares; (iii) option for simplified real VAT regime if turnover thresholds allow; and (iv) election for treatment as a separate taxable entity for VAT on certain joint terminal arrangements. The SAS cannot elect partnership-style pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold applies to foreign suppliers not established in France (obligation from the first euro of taxable turnover). Domestic micro-enterprises benefit from the franchise en base: EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services (2024 thresholds). The port stevedoring service generally falls under the EUR 37,500 threshold, but the actual SAS terminal operator, being a commercial entity of scale, is normally registered regardless of the domestic threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting under the Facturation Électronique reform. All taxable persons must accept e-invoices through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) by 1 September 2026; large and mid-size enterprises must issue e-invoices via the PPF or an accredited partner platform (PDP) by that date, and all taxable persons by 1 September 2027. Invoices must be transmitted in structured electronic formats (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) through certified PDPs using API connections. No fiscal stamp is applied by DGFiP; rather, clearance is achieved through near-real-time transmission of invoice data to the tax authority, supported by a checksum generated by the platform. VAT on imported goods continues to be settled under the customs electronic declaration systems (DELTA).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for export of goods from the EU is mandatory under Article 262-1 of the CGI where the supplier is a taxable person, the goods are physically dispatched outside the EU, and the departure is evidenced by customs export declaration within the statutory deadlines. Services directly related to the exported goods—including stevedoring, dock handling, and bunkering at marine bulk terminals—qualify for zero-rating under Article 275 of the CGI if the service is rendered to the consignor or consignee of the exported goods and is directly linked to the export dispatch. Intra-EU dispatches are subject to a separate exemption regime and require the buyer's valid EU VAT ID, not the export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en douane d'exportation / DAE) with the validated export exit confirmation from DGDDI
Bill of Lading (B/L) or equivalent ocean transport document showing cargo lifted at a French port and consigned to a destination outside the EU
Commercial invoice issued to the foreign purchaser, stating the export or customs reference
Original contract or service agreement for stevedoring/terminal services demonstrating direct linkage to an export cargo
Proof of physical exit from the EU (e.g., destination port arrival certificate, customs-scale note, or P&I survey confirmation)
Bank statement or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of the export consideration and, where applicable, the inward remittance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is heavily scrutinized by DGFiP and DGDDI during VAT audits. If a taxpayer fails to produce documentary evidence within the audit period, the administration will reassess VAT at the standard rate and apply interest de retard (0.20% per month) plus penalties of 10% to 80% under Articles 1728 and 1729 of the CGI, increasing to 100% for organized fraud or abusive maneuvers (manœuvres frauduleuses). Criminal sanctions for tax evasion can reach 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 75,000 fine. Where zero-rating is invalid, the input VAT deducted on goods and services attributable to the export is retroactively clawed back, and the tax representative, if any, may be held jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank) together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the French Monetary and Financial Code; the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) supervises credit institutions and payment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies the EU Treaty free movement of capital provisions. The euro is fully convertible and no prior exchange-control authorization is required for current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance and dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders are freely transferable through registered credit institutions, subject to standard corporate tax and, if applicable, 25% dividend withholding tax unless treaty relief or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption is available. Beneficial ownership declarations and banque de France statistical reporting obligations must be observed for all cross-border financial flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation to surrender or convert export proceeds into euros in France. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in eurozone bank accounts. However, all cross-border transfers exceeding EUR 50,000 per calendar month must be reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistical purposes on form FDEB (or through the bank's electronic reporting channel). Commercial shipments must be supported by inbound and outbound customs declarations and freight/shipping evidence for treasury reconciliation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EU-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions operating under PSD II, such as Qonto, MangoPay, and various ACPR-licensed platforms, for day-to-day operational liquidity. Legal constraints require that the EMI hold segregated client funds in a French or EEA credit institution, and that the EMI registers with the ACPR or another EEA competent authority. A licensed stevedoring terminal should not rely solely on an EMI for statutory port-authority clearing, escrow requirements, or complex trade settlement; use EMIs as supplemental payment circuits only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC with legally compliant video identification is accepted by French banks under the transposed Fourth and Fifth EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives. Physical appearance of directors is generally not mandatory for standard low-risk corporates if the constitutional documents are notarized and apostilled. However, for entities with complex ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) chains or non-EU resident shareholders, French compliance officers frequently require a physical or remote interview with at least one senior signatory and the UBO at a French bank branch or an accredited KYC agent. Recommended plan: prepare apostilled certificates of incorporation, board resolutions, a clean UBO register, and audited group financial statements before the onboarding interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds or wealth for the initial capital injection from a non-EU parent or holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited parent financial statements, latest interim group accounts, notarised equity subscription deed, bank reference letters, contractual evidence of the commercial purpose, source-of-funds explanatory memorandum, tax-residence certificate, and a sworn declaration from each capital contributor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows associated with sanctioned jurisdictions or designated port counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening policy, charter party and stevedoring service agreement with compliance clauses, current denied-party screening reports, Incoterms-based invoices, end-user declarations, flag vessel registration data, and documentary evidence that port stops and cargo origin/destination comply with EU restrictive measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the French Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and bank-requested beneficial ownership data.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC register updated in accordance with Article L.561-2-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, certified chain-of-ownership diagram, passport copies of all natural-person UBOs, notarised shareholder registry, and an RCS extract dated within the last three months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Involvement of politically exposed persons (PEPs), state-owned port authorities, or sovereign wealth entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP assessment report, public tender concession agreement, state concession contract, irrevocable payment guarantees, and correspondence evidencing arms-length commercial terms for the stevedoring concession.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 / MT202 through a French licensed credit institution. The payment narrative must state 'Injection de capitaux' and identify the corporate purpose (e.g., 'Constitution / augmentation de capital'). Attach the signed equity subscription deed, statutory resolution of shareholders, and Article 1 EU Regulation 2023/1113 travel-rule information. For a capital increase, the receiving bank requires RCS filing proof. The correct balance-of-payments classification for the transfer is equity capital, reported as 'F1 – Participations et actions' to the Banque de France. Escrowed injections should be first settled on a segregated capital escrow account, verified against the notarial deed, and only then swept to the operational account after registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic and euro-area operational payments use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT). International trade settlements for stevedoring equipment, bulk-cargo tariffs, and subcontractor mobilisation use SWIFT MT103 alongside the Commercial Letter of Credit (ICC UCP 600) mechanism. For statutory port authority dues, settlement must be routed through the port community system (e.g., S.N.A.P. at Le Havre or Tracy at Marseille) integrated with the corporate treasury bank account. Purpose codes should follow ISO 20022: '110' for import/export of goods, 'Hra' for harbour dues, and 'INTC' or 'TANG' for intercompany disbursements. All outbound MT103 instructions must pass screening and include the precise invoice and contract reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign-exchange forwards for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and euro-area safe cross-currency pairs, with standard tenors of up to 12 months.
Foreign-exchange swaps and rolling FX forwards under an ISDA 2002 master agreement with a credit support annex.
European-style currency options to cap port revenue transaction cost volatility.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the underlying currency is not freely deliverable outside the eurozone, subject to EMIR reporting and appropriate ISDA credit support.

Cross-currency swaps combining interest rate and currency basis flows, permissible for operational treasury hedging when fully documented under EMIR.M. and cleared through an eligible central counterparty where required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; the articles may regulate the approval procedure, but cannot generally extend the statutory six-month period without court relief
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court injunction, daily coercive penalty, director liability, and fines generally up to EUR 9,000 for failure to prepare or approve accounts; no automatic administrative strike-off solely from missing approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and required accompanying documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the Guichet unique managed by INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; two months where filed electronically. Filing includes applicable accounts, management report or exemption statement, auditor report where applicable, and profit-allocation resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine generally EUR 1,500, increasing to EUR 3,000 for repeat offences, court injunction and daily penalty; persistent registry non-compliance may support administrative removal or other RCS measures, but no fixed automatic strike-off period applies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and tax package, Form No. 2065 and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration, Direction générale des Finances publiques
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day following 1 May for a calendar-year company, unless a different electronically published deadline applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally 0.20% per month plus a 10% surcharge, increasing in aggravated cases; tax reassessment, penalties and collection measures may follow; no direct automatic strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory audit appointment and auditor reporting, where mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders or sole shareholder; auditor report filed with annual accounts where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor appointment must be made when statutory thresholds or group conditions are met, normally before approval of the relevant financial statements; audit report accompanies the accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a mandatory auditor may constitute a criminal offence, expose the legal representative to fines and liability, and invalidate or impair statutory approval and filing processes; no automatic strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information review and change filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet unique managed by INPI and the competent commercial court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual beneficial-owner confirmation filing; review annually and file each change or inaccuracy within 30 days of the change or discovery, subject to applicable registry rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and daily penalty, criminal exposure for failure or false information, and possible restrictions on registry services; no automatic annual strike-off deadline

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of three thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional obligations may apply to parent companies, controlled companies and qualifying groups at lower group thresholds. Voluntary appointment is permitted.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations for statutory individual accounts. IFRS is generally relevant to qualifying consolidated accounts, particularly listed groups, and is not the default framework for an unlisted SAS individual account set.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for an SAS. The company must conduct an annual internal verification of ownership and control information and promptly update the beneficial-owner filing after any change, generally within 30 days. Shareholding transfers must also be recorded in the securities movement register and individual shareholder accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and movements in securities
Register or minute book of shareholder and sole-shareholder decisions
Register or minute book of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies where maintained under the articles
Accounting books and supporting records required under French commercial law

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 600-2500 per year for a standard registered office and corporate administration package; France does not generally require a separate annual registered-agent renewal fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3000-15000 for a small or medium SAS subject to mandatory statutory audit; complex, regulated or group audits may exceed USD 20000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit, innovation tax credit, and other preferential deductions for qualifying expenditures; no specific tax holidays for bulk port stevedoring operations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat (Formulaire 1201) filed electronically through the French tax authorities portal at impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Three months after the close of the fiscal year for standard filers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Starting point for taxable income calculation including all revenues and expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only French-source income; permanent establishment adjustments required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: After applying deductions, exemptions, and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply any available incentives or treaty-based reliefs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €75 per day, capped at €10,000; penalties for erroneous declarations up to 80% of additional tax due; potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent filings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for qualifying corporate distributions under domestic law and most treaties
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and relevant forms to invoke DTA benefits; administrative process via French tax portal with supporting documentation
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: typically 0% under DTAs; Interest: 0% under EU Interest and Royalties Directive and bilateral treaties (standard domestic rate 12.8%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million in consolidated annual turnover to trigger mandatory local file and master file documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France enforces economic substance requirements primarily through DAC6 reporting and national anti-avoidance rules; operating entities such as port terminals must demonstrate adequate physical presence and operational activities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable profits or false statements in tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions including up to 5 years imprisonment and fines of up to 80% of the evaded tax amount or €80,000, whichever is greater
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, fines, disqualification from corporate offices, and possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a company without genuine business activities or economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €75,000 and potential liquidation of the entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Fines and civil liability for management errors leading to tax fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or apply arm's length transfer pricing documentation or adjustments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of €10,000 per day of delay and retroactive tax reassessments with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability for unpaid tax debts and possible personal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify or report suspicious cross-border financial transactions or profit flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 5% of annual turnover, and potential criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment up to 2 years, fines, and disqualification
